classification.difficultyReason: Apply the central-angle theorem and explain how the semicircle theorem follows from it.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10, first circle on the left
spec.description: Circle with centre O, radii OA and OB, and chords AC and BC. The central angle above O is labelled 140 degrees. Ordinary source blue geometry is rendered black in house style.
spec.mathematics: A, B and C lie on the circle; the non-reflex angle AOB is 140 degrees and C lies on the complementary arc AB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied central angle is visible; the requested angle ACB is not labelled.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10, second circle on the right
spec.description: Circle with centre O on diameter AB, and chords AC and BC. The straight central angle above AB is labelled 180 degrees. Ordinary source blue geometry is rendered black in house style.
spec.mathematics: AB is a diameter through O; C lies on the circle below AB; angle AOB is 180 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied straight central angle is visible; the requested angle ACB is not labelled.

children.label: a
children.prompt: For the first circle shown, find $\angle ACB$.

answer.worked:
The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ACB &= \frac{140^\circ}{2}\\\angle ACB &= 70^\circ\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: For the second circle shown, find $\angle ACB$.

answer.worked:
The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ACB &= \frac{180^\circ}{2}\\\angle ACB &= 90^\circ\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Explain why “The angle in a semicircle is $90^\circ$” is a special case of “The angle at the centre of a circle is twice the angle at the circumference when standing on the same arc.”

answer.short: A diameter gives an angle of $180^\circ$ at the centre, so the angle at the circumference is $180^\circ\div2=90^\circ$.
answer.worked: When $AB$ is a diameter, $\angle AOB=180^\circ$. The angle at the circumference standing on the same semicircular arc is half this angle, so $\angle ACB=90^\circ$.
